title: GeoMix: Towards Geometry-Aware Data Augmentation

problem.claim: Limited labeled data creates challenges for image classification and graph learning tasks.

gap.claim: Mixup has rarely been explored in graph learning because graph irregularity and connectivity make it difficult to create connections for synthetic nodes in node classification.

contributions.claim: GeoMix is a simple and interpretable Mixup approach that uses in-place graph editing.
GeoMix uses geometry information to interpolate features and labels with nearby-neighborhood information, generating synthetic nodes and establishing their connections.
The paper provides theoretical analysis of using geometry information for node Mixup and emphasizes locality enhancement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GeoMix achieves state-of-the-art results on a wide variety of standard datasets with limited labeled data.
The authors report that GeoMix significantly improves the generalization capability of underlying GNNs across challenging out-of-distribution generalization tasks.
The authors report that the method is lightweight.

narrative_sequence.summary: Mixup addresses data scarcity by interpolating features and labels.
Graph learning presents unresolved Mixup challenges because graph structure is irregular and connected, especially when creating synthetic-node connections.
GeoMix applies geometry-aware interpolation and in-place graph editing to generate and connect synthetic nodes.
The paper analyzes the rationale for geometry-aware node Mixup and highlights locality enhancement.
The authors report strong standard-dataset results and improved out-of-distribution generalization for underlying GNNs.

source_observation.claim: Synthetic graph data requires both feature-label interpolation and a strategy for establishing graph connections.

interpretation.claim: Data augmentation for structured data should preserve or construct relevant structural relationships, not only interpolate attributes.

application.claim: When augmenting graph data, incorporate local geometry or neighborhood information into synthetic-node construction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether geometry-aware augmentation is beneficial for graph tasks beyond the reported node-classification and out-of-distribution settings.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The theoretical assumptions and guarantees are not provided.
The precise graph-editing procedure and interpolation formula are not provided.
